title: Bunny Doesn't Want to Sleep
summary: Night has fallen over the forest, but little Bunny still has so many jobs, ideas and games that keep sleep far away. A funny, soothing rhyming story about trying to put off bedtime, and about the gentle way to let go and drift into the land of dreams.
pages:
It's late, very late, the whole forest's asleep,
but Bunny keeps tossing, not tired, not a peep.
He bounces on the bed with a hop and a spring,
his eyes open wide, not a yawn, not a thing.
His ears stand up tall like antennas in the air,
and Bunny tells the room: "I won't stop singing, I swear!"

"Bunny has things to do!" he says good and loud,
"No time to doze, not now, not ever, no how!"
He lines up his pinecones in a row on the floor,
by size, by smell, by how wide, and much more.
He dances and whistles and calls to the room:
"Just one second, one minute! My ear hears the quiet's tune!"

The pinecones are resting, but look what he's found:
a funny little shadow on the wall, dancing round!
Bunny lifts up an arm and twirls his paws,
and teaches the shadow to hop and to cry, just because.
He laughs and he giggles and makes a silly face,
for a bunny this stubborn won't stop all night in this place!

The shadow gets tired and smears on the wall,
so Bunny decides to get to know his pillow, that's all.
He counts every wrinkle that runs like a trail:
one, two, three, and five little hills without fail!
He finds eighty in all, and two more in the corner,
and announces he's not one bit sleepy, not a yawner!

Maybe you can yawn backwards, from the outside in?
Bunny tries blowing, and a deep sound comes from within.
But a giant yawn suddenly comes rolling along,
as big and as sweet as a wave in a dream-song.
He tries to stop it, but his mouth opens wide,
and suddenly his thoughts start drifting aside.

Outside a breeze blows, whispering slow,
playing a tune through the oak branches below.
A cricket sings a lullaby, soft and deep,
and the leaves rustle gently, a hug before sleep.
Bunny stops for a moment, his ears start to rest:
what a quiet night, with the falling leaves' gentle beat at its best.

He asks himself in the softest of whispers:
"Where do all the dreams go so peacefully, like sisters?
If open eyes can't see anything at all,
maybe the great magic is made in the dark, after all?"
Bunny sits up and wonders, so curious and new,
and feels a sweet calm creeping into his heart, too.

He decides to try a special experiment right there:
to close his right eye, then the other one with care,
just to peek at the sweet little secret that waits
so quietly for him, near and far, past the gates.
One eye closes up, and the second gives in,
into a soft picture that touches his heart deep within.

The blanket becomes like a cloud, soft and warm,
and each thought is wrapped up in wool, safe from harm.
His breathing slows down, his body relaxes too,
like a boat gently floating on a pond calm and blue.
And Bunny discovers the most beautiful trip
begins when you let your tired body just slip.

His ears are resting on the cozy pillow,
and Bunny sails off to a wonderland, mellow.
No more "one minute", no more "one second", no more,
just a dream that's better than any wish before.
A smile on his lips shines bright as the light,
and the night watches over him like a song through the night.
